rich_summary: Lomasa narrates to Yudhishthira the origins of the legend that will eventually lead to the descent of the Ganga. King Sagara of the Ikshvaku line performs severe austerities to obtain children. Siva grants a strange boon: one wife will bear a single heir who will continue the lineage, while the other will produce sixty thousand sons who will ultimately perish together. The sons grow powerful but arrogant and violent. During Sagara’s horse sacrifice, the sacred horse disappears, and the princes dig through the earth and the ocean in their search, causing immense destruction. They eventually find the horse near the sage Kapila but rashly attack him and are burned to ashes by his fiery glance. Sagara’s grandson Ansuman respectfully approaches Kapila, retrieves the horse, and learns that a future descendant—Bhagiratha—will bring the Ganga to earth to purify the dead princes. The episode explains the moral contrast between arrogance and humility and sets up the famous Ganga myth.

highlight_spans.why: Introduces the question about how Bhagiratha’s lineage would provide the occasion for refilling the ocean, framing the mythic narrative that follows.
Siva’s prophecy that one wife will bear sixty thousand sons destined to perish together while the other bears the true heir—this prophecy drives the entire tragedy.
The destructive digging of the earth and ocean by Sagara’s sons, illustrating their reckless arrogance and the suffering they cause.
The pivotal moment when the sage Kapila burns the princes to ashes with his fiery power after they rush at him in ignorance.
Kapila’s prophecy to Ansuman that a future descendant will bring the Ganga to purify the fallen sons, linking this tragedy to the sacred origin of the river.

top_scenes.scene_text: The sixty thousand princes furiously digging into the earth and the dried ocean with spades while terrified creatures and serpents flee amid chaos.
The radiant sage Kapila seated in blazing meditation as the reckless sons of Sagara rush toward him and are consumed by sudden flames.
Prince Ansuman humbly bowing before the luminous sage Kapila beside the recovered sacrificial horse in the depths of the earth.
